answer: Make trust expensive to rent and cheap to verify: each agent locks a deposit that scales with the trade volume it wants, and earns a reputation score that decays when idle. Like layers of shale, a real deposit history is hard to fake in bulk — every identity must fund itself and wait out the same slow climb. Clean reputations bloom like a lotus, visibly and gradually, while Sybil clusters leave thin, identical trails. Peers read that signal before trading, so a flood of clones cannot buy trust at zero cost.
